references.text: The Lord says to Moses that he must go down because the people have acted corruptly - same wording and situation as in Exodus 32:7
Moses predicts that the people will become corrupt after his death, using the same Hebrew root (שחת) for corruption
Describes the people as corrupt, with the same theme of Israel's apostasy and corruption
Uses the same Hebrew word (שחת) to say that the earth was corrupt before God's face
The Lord says he has come down - in contrast to Moses now being told to go down; same expression for going down (ירד)
The Lord commands Moses to go down from the mountain, using the same command (לך רד)
The people refer to Moses as the one who brought them up out of Egypt - same phrasing as God uses in verse 7
Moses responds by calling Israel 'your people' back to God, in reply to God calling them 'your people' to Moses
Israel has forsaken the Lord who brought them out of Egypt - same theme of apostasy from God who brought them out
Stephen quotes this event and describes how the people rejected Moses and made the golden calf
Links the warning about sin directly to its consequence: God's distance from the people.
A prophetic parallel showing the people's persistent tendency to break covenant, both in the past (the golden calf) and the future.
Specifies the character of the people's sin ('stiff-necked') and the consequence of the breach mentioned in 32:7.
